atlases.assemble: repeat every 16px to span the gap. EVERY tile MUST use the SAME frame index: the profile is periodic in x with period 16 only for a fixed frame phase, so advancing the frame per tile jumps the phase at each join and steps the contour at every seam. Flow comes from the whole run advancing together.
atlases.seamRule: same frame index across all tiles of one run

breathStream.note: The dragon’s attack is a CONTINUOUS stream that must always reach its target. Assemble it, do not stretch a single cone: root at the maw, ceil((dist-28-19)/16) mid tiles, tip on the target face. All parts of one run share ONE frame index — that is what keeps the joins invisible; the pattern shifting frame to frame is the flow. A continuous stream needs no separate impact burst: the tip part IS the contact effect, so fire impact_burn once at onset at most.
breathStream.seamRule: same frame index across root, all mid tiles and tip

targeting.giant: walls first with the melee slab (state: attack), then defences from range with the boulder (state: throw)
targeting.dragon: continuous fire stream at any range (state: breath) — never falls short
targeting.cannon: ground troops within range; aim then fire then reload
targeting.mortar: ground troops at range — high-arc splash. Cannot hit what is close: the arc means a minimum range, unlike the cannon.

attachments: Emitter points are PUBLISHED per atlas cell (see `emitters` on the dragon breath/spit and cannon idle/aim/fire/reload atlases) because "pin it to the mouth" is not a spec. They are projected from the same rig node and camera the sprite is drawn with, so they cannot drift from the art. The mortar publishes `emitters.muzzle` the same way the cannon does.
mortarNote: The mortar is built as a RING, not a tube. Every other defence reads as a line (cannon = barrel out, towers = vertical shaft); a near-upright bombard presents its open bore to the elev-42 camera as a big dark ellipse inside a bronze lip, which is a silhouette nothing else in the set has and which survives down to 24px. Aim reads as the bombard LEANING toward its target, not as it pointing — a near-vertical weapon swept through a full circle would look identical in all eight aims.
